precepts.text: Evil-merodach lifted up the head of Jehoiachin after thirty-seven years in prison, set his throne above the kings with him in Babylon and gave him a continual allowance all the days of his life; Jeconiah got mercy and status in captivity, but he was a captive.
precepts.point: They slew his sons before his eyes, put out his eyes, and carried him bound to Babylon; Zedekiah was the last king of Judah, and his heirs were gone.

note.label: The Nativity: the Bloodline, Birthright, & the Messiah

precepts.why:
Zedekiah rebelled like his brother and his nephew did. He tried to run away and got caught in the plains of Jericho, and they killed his kids in front of him first, then took his eyes out, bound him and locked him up in Babylon. At this point there are no more kings of Judah; Zedekiah was the last one. His sons are gone, his heirs are gone. So who's left?

Read on: “in the seven and thirtieth year of the captivity of Jehoiachin king of Judah”, “Evil–merodach king of Babylon in the year that he began to reign did lift up the head of Jehoiachin king of Judah out of prison; And he spake kindly to him, and set his throne above the throne of the kings that were with him in Babylon”. Jehoiachin had been locked up between 36 and 37 years. Then he “changed his prison garments: and he did eat bread continually before him all the days of his life.” His allowance was a continual allowance, a daily rate for every day: Babylon gave him a job and status.

Jehoiachin is Jeconiah, and he is the Jechonias of Matthew 1:11. He got some mercy in captivity, but was he a king anymore at this point? No. He was a king, but now he was a captive in Babylon, receiving wages and some status.

And in Babylon he had children: “the sons of Jeconiah; Assir, Salathiel his son”. Salathiel is Shealtiel, the father of Zerubbabel, whose name means born in Babylon. That is where the line of the kings of Judah went on after Zedekiah's sons were slain: through a captive king in Babylon.

note.label: The Nativity: the Bloodline, Birthright, & the Messiah

points: In the ninth year of Zedekiah's reign Nebuchadnezzar came with all his host against Jerusalem, pitched against it, and built forts round about it.

note.label: 2 Kings 25: The Fall of Jerusalem and the Burning of the Temple

points: The city was besieged until the eleventh year of Zedekiah, and the famine prevailed in the city.

note.label: 2 Kings 25: The Fall of Jerusalem and the Burning of the Temple

points: Because the city was besieged no food, water, or goods could get in, so there was no bread for the people of the land.

note.label: 2 Kings 25: The Fall of Jerusalem and the Burning of the Temple

points: The city was broken up and the men of war fled by night by the way of the gate between two walls by the king's garden, while the Chaldeans were round about the city.

note.label: 2 Kings 25: The Fall of Jerusalem and the Burning of the Temple

points: The army pursued the king, overtook him in the plains of Jericho, and his army was scattered from him, and they took him to the king of Babylon at Riblah, where judgment was given upon him.

note.label: 2 Kings 25: The Fall of Jerusalem and the Burning of the Temple

points: They slew Zedekiah's sons before his eyes, then put out his eyes, bound him with fetters of brass, and carried him to Babylon, just as Jeremiah had warned him.

note.label: 2 Kings 25: The Fall of Jerusalem and the Burning of the Temple

points: In the fifth month of the nineteenth year of Nebuchadnezzar, Nebuzaradan the captain of the guard came to Jerusalem.

note.label: 2 Kings 25: The Fall of Jerusalem and the Burning of the Temple

points: He burnt the house of the Lord, the king's house, and every great man's house, and the army broke down the walls of Jerusalem round about.

note.label: 2 Kings 25: The Fall of Jerusalem and the Burning of the Temple

points: He carried away the rest of the people and the fugitives, but left the poor of the land to be vinedressers and husbandmen, since the poor could not fend for themselves.

note.label: 2 Kings 25: The Fall of Jerusalem and the Burning of the Temple

points: The Chaldeans broke in pieces the pillars of brass, the bases, and the brasen sea that were in the house of the Lord, and carried the brass to Babylon because it was valuable.

note.label: 2 Kings 25: The Fall of Jerusalem and the Burning of the Temple

points: They took away the pots, shovels, snuffers, spoons, and vessels of brass, and the firepans and bowls of gold and silver the captain of the guard took away.

note.label: 2 Kings 25: The Fall of Jerusalem and the Burning of the Temple

points: The two pillars, one sea, and the bases Solomon had made were of brass without weight, the one pillar eighteen cubits high with a brasen chapiter, wreathen work, and pomegranates round about.

note.label: 2 Kings 25: The Fall of Jerusalem and the Burning of the Temple

points: The captain of the guard took Seraiah the chief priest, Zephaniah the second priest, and the three keepers of the door.

note.label: 2 Kings 25: The Fall of Jerusalem and the Burning of the Temple

points: He took an officer over the men of war, five men in the king's presence, the principal scribe of the host, and threescore men of the people found in the city.

note.label: 2 Kings 25: The Fall of Jerusalem and the Burning of the Temple

points: Nebuzaradan brought them to the king of Babylon at Riblah, and the king smote and slew them there; so Judah was carried away out of their land.

note.label: 2 Kings 25: The Fall of Jerusalem and the Burning of the Temple

points: Over the people left in the land Nebuchadnezzar made Gedaliah the son of Ahikam, the son of Shaphan, governor.

note.label: 2 Kings 25: The Fall of Jerusalem and the Burning of the Temple

points: Gedaliah counselled the captains and their men not to fear to serve the Chaldeans but to dwell in the land and serve the king of Babylon, and it would be well with them.

note.label: 2 Kings 25: The Fall of Jerusalem and the Burning of the Temple

points: But Ishmael the son of Nethaniah, of the royal seed, came with ten men and smote Gedaliah and the Jews and Chaldeans with him, and the people fled to Egypt for fear of the Chaldeans, killing a man who gave wise counsel.

note.label: 2 Kings 25: The Fall of Jerusalem and the Burning of the Temple

points: In the thirty seventh year of the captivity of Jehoiachin, Evilmerodach king of Babylon lifted up his head out of prison and spake kindly to him.

note.label: 2 Kings 25: The Fall of Jerusalem and the Burning of the Temple

points: He set his throne above the thrones of the other kings in Babylon, changed his prison garments, and let him eat bread continually before him all the days of his life.

note.label: 2 Kings 25: The Fall of Jerusalem and the Burning of the Temple

points: Jehoiachin was given a continual daily allowance for the rest of his life, a mercy shown at the very end of the account.
